name: Tienosuchus
isnote: Traditionally placed in the Thoracosaurinae, now regarded as a paraphyletic assemblage of basal gavialoids; the fragmentary material allows no finer placement (English Wikipedia).
sum: Tienosuchus is a dubious gavialoid crocodilian known from a tooth and some postcranial remains from the Eocene of Hunan, China.
wsnote: The sources consulted do not give the body length.
holotype: A tooth and postcranial remains collected in Hunan (Young 1948); Catalogue number not given in the sources consulted.
material: One tooth and some postcranial bones.
biology: The sources consulted give no evidence of diet or habits.
author: Young 1948

sources.text: C. -C. Young. 1948. Fossil crocodiles in China, with notes on dinosaurian remains associated with the Kansu crocodiles. Bulletin of the Geological Society of China 28(3-4):255-288
